_comment: English body for open-webui; generated from the Chinese dossier and official pages, not a literal translation.

axes.model_access: No built-in model: connect Ollama and any local or cloud OpenAI-compatible API, plus providers such as Anthropic. Credentials stay in your instance. Provider coverage and version differences follow the official Connect a Provider documentation.
axes.runtime: Self-hosted web app: Docker, Python, Kubernetes or a desktop app. The front end is a browser; inference and data stay on your machine or server by default and do not pass through Open WebUI’s cloud.
axes.local_files: Upload documents, images and code; knowledge bases and vector stores live in your instance. Open Terminal gives an agent a controlled shell and filesystem to read, write, run scripts and return artefacts to the conversation.
axes.background: Automations can run prompts on a schedule, and long tasks run in the instance background. Whether they continue after shutdown depends on where the instance is deployed; the platform does not host your execution environment.
axes.tools: Python Tools and Functions, Skills, OpenAPI and MCP (the official mcpo bridge turns an MCP server into OpenAPI); built-in code execution, web search and image-generation plugin surfaces.
axes.context: The context window is set by the connected model. The instance provides conversation history, Memory, knowledge-base retrieval and a full-text injection switch; cross-project long-term memory boundaries were kept at the official category level.
axes.permissions: Multi-user RBAC: roles, groups, per-model and per-resource access, SSO/OIDC/LDAP, SCIM, MFA and API keys. Data and logs stay on your infrastructure; admins can disable telemetry and external services.
axes.fit: Fits: teams that want one private chat entry point over local and cloud models, with RAG, tool use, multi-user permissions and a self-hosted data boundary. Does not fit: zero-ops SaaS, or procurement that requires a vendor SLA.

runs: This site has not completed measured task runs for this entry. We checked the official product, help and terms pages and recorded capabilities, data paths and known limits. Suggested checks: the real tier boundaries, the data-retention default, and one end-to-end task with representative content.

related: Open WebUI can front Ollama; it adds a full workspace, RBAC and retrieval on top of the runtime.
Open WebUI and Dify overlap on RAG and assistants: Open WebUI is a chat workspace, Dify is a workflow and app builder.
